summary: Lincoln T. Zacconi works in philosophy and Indology. He completed a specialization in neuro-psycho-pedagogy at Faculdade da Aldeia de Carapicuíba in 2016 and pursued master's studies at the University of São Paulo in 2017.

Linda Hogan is a religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Maynooth and Trinity College Dublin (PhD 1991). She held posts at Chester and Leeds before serving at Trinity College Dublin as lecturer, Chair of Ecumenics, and Vice-Provost (2011–2016).

Linda Jean LaMacchia is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where she studied under doctoral supervisor David M. Knipe (attested 2001).

Linda Learman works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. Her academic training includes doctoral supervision under Robert P. Weller and postdoctoral mentorship under Peter N. Gregory (both attested 2005).
Linda Penkower is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed her PhD at Columbia University in 1993 and was an attested research fellow at Taisho University in 1983.
Linda York Leach (1942–2006) was a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. She studied at the University of Michigan and earned her PhD from Case Western Reserve University in 1978.
Lindsay G. McCune is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. McCune studied under MA supervisor Bryan J. Cuevas as well as teachers Kathleen M. Erndl and John Corrigan.
Lindy Li Mark (born 1932) is a scholar of Sinology and anthropology. She held posts as professor of anthropology at California State University, East Bay, and at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Ling Ji is a Sinologist who completed a PhD at the National University of Singapore (attested 2014) under the doctoral supervision of Yuet-Keung Lo.

Linnart Mäll (1938–2010) was an Estonian scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tartu (~1957–1962) and under Bidia Dandaron (~1965–1972), later holding a post at Tartu from ~1966 to 2010.
Linus Klemp works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Affiliated with the University of Copenhagen, he held a PhD position there in 2025 and is attested as a PhD Fellow in 2026.
Lionel Burton Burrows (1883–1970) was an Indologist and linguist who was educated at St. Paul's School in Darjeeling and at Elphinstone College.

Lionel David Barnett (1871–1960) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Cambridge and Liverpool. He served as Assistant Keeper at the British Museum (1899–1936, 1948), Professor of Sanskrit at UCL (1906–1917), and Lecturer at SOAS (1917–1948).
Lionel James Trotter (1827–1912) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Charterhouse School (~1840–1846) and Merton College (~1846–1847).

Lionel Obadia (born 1968) is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Lille (1997). He held posts at INALCO, KU Leuven, EPHE, Lille 3, and Lumière University Lyon 2.

Liqian Liu (1910–2008) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at West China Union University (~1946–1949), the Ethnic Publishing House, and the translation administration department of the State Council of the People's Republic of China.

Lisa Grumbach works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She held a post at Stanford University (attested 1996) and has served as an assistant professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Lisa N. Owen is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. She earned her MA and PhD from the University of Texas at Austin under Janice Leoshko, and also studied under Walter M. Spink in 1995.

Lise Menn (born 1941) is a linguist who studied at Swarthmore College, Brandeis University, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. She held an academic post at the University of Colorado Boulder from 1986 to 2007.

Lita Peipina is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned an MA at the University of Oslo (attested 2008) under the supervision of Jens Braarvig, and also studied under Jens-Uwe Hartmann.
